title: Undo removal details
blurb: Archive, Trash, and Move accumulate completed changes across batches in one removal Undo session until restored or cleared. Details, beside Undo, opens a checklist with the subject, sender, and action (archive, trash, or move), plus the destination when it is known. Rows also show the mailbox label/address when the session spans multiple accounts. Each checkbox keeps its subject as its name; its description includes the sender, action, destination and mailbox when shown. Select all or Clear selection, then Undo selected. Clear selection only unchecks rows; it does not discard Undo. Select all and Clear keep Details open. Undo all and Undo selected ask for confirmation with the reviewed change count and actions. When reviewing one change, the confirmation shows the message sender and subject when available. Cancel or Escape makes no mailbox changes. New completions are not added to an open confirmation; a retired or changed selection must be reviewed again. The status chip only shows or hides the notice, anchored at the bottom-right. Details stays open as batches and late completions join, preserving surviving selection, scroll and checkbox focus; new rows start unchecked. Escape closes it and returns focus. Restore controls wait until pending restores settle, and unreported rows stay available. Mark as read keeps its own Undo and does not replace a removal Undo, including a pending removal. Different changes to the same message stay separate: select one change per message and restore its latest change first. Provider identity checks can refuse an obsolete restore. Outbox undo send is separate and is not in this checklist. Settlements belonging to a retired session cannot revive its checklist. A change restored before the rest of its bulk request finishes stays out of Undo and does not clear its reopened message or selection, even after all changes have been restored.
